title: appname.aiSession.v1 — copilot session, grant-identity binding, data-egress, and tamper-evident audit (ENGINEERING-SPEC.md Part 53 §53.4.7, §53.10, §53.14; review actions AI-001/AI-002)

path.description: append-only JSONL beside the session store (§31 layout); lines validate against #/$defs/auditEntry

clientIdentity.description: §53.4.7 client identity tuple — part of every grant fingerprint. v5.5 (AI-ID-001): the tuple is cryptographically anchored via installationId + executableFingerprint; name/version/transport remain for display and diagnostics but are never the binding identity alone.

transport.description: how the client reaches the tool layer (§53.13.3); http_remote is loopback-token-gated

installationId.description: AI-ID-001 (v5.5): per-installation random UUID minted at first run and stored in the OS keychain — a name/version/transport tuple alone is impersonable by any client using the same strings; this anchors the tuple to one concrete installation.

executableFingerprint.description: AI-ID-001 (v5.5): blake3-256 of the client executable's code-signature identity (platform signing certificate/team-id + binary digest for external clients; the app's own binary digest for the builtin panel and in-process adapters). A persistent grant binds to THIS, so a renamed or tampered executable can never inherit it.

allOf.$comment: AI-005 (enforced): kind determines the permitted transport — the builtin panel and the OpenAI/Anthropic tool-calling adapters are in-process components of appname-ai; an MCP stdio client is stdio; an MCP HTTP client is loopback or (token-gated) remote. An invalid combination cannot validate merely because duplicated transport fields happen to agree.

providerRef.description: §53.6 provider the copilot drives; secrets live in the OS keychain, never here

endpointRef.description: opaque keychain handle (§53.6.4) — never a URL with embedded secrets, never persisted in documents/exports

endpointFingerprint.description: blake3-256 hex (64 lowercase hex chars — AI-008: a meaningful digest, not free text) of the canonical endpoint tuple (provider.kind ‖ URL scheme ‖ host ‖ port ‖ path ‖ modelId), so a scheme/port/path/account change re-fingerprints; the grant-binding anchor for remote endpoints (§53.4.7); absent for local_llamacpp

credentialPrincipalFingerprint.description: AI-ID-002 (v5.5): blake3-256 of the credential PRINCIPAL tuple (provider account id ‖ organization/tenant id ‖ project id — the identity the API key resolves to, NEVER the secret itself; resolved at key registration via the provider's identity endpoint and stored beside the keychain handle). Swapping API keys on the same endpoint changes the principal and re-fingerprints, so a persistent grant cannot silently transfer across accounts.

allOf.$comment: AI-003/AI-ID-002 (enforced): any REMOTE provider MUST carry the endpointFingerprint, the modelId, AND the credentialPrincipalFingerprint — a persistent grant survives neither endpoint, model, nor account/tenant/project substitution. Only local_llamacpp is exempt.

grant.description: §53.4.7 — a grant is BOUND, not ambient: every field below is part of the identity a persistent grant must re-match, or it downgrades to a fresh session prompt.
grant.$comment: Temporal invariants (runtime + V35-enforced; cross-field date-time ordering is not expressible in JSON Schema draft 2020-12): grantedAt < expiresAt when present; grantedAt <= revokedAt when present. The timestamp PATTERN below rejects malformed values at the schema layer; the ORDER is checked by the validator's property harness (V35) and the transcript runner's state machine (V36), and enforced by the runtime. v5.5 (AI-003): the three docScope binding branches are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE oneOf alternatives — a grant has exactly one canonical binding representation; a foreign id (workspaceId on a document grant, any id on a global grant) is rejected, so two semantically-identical grants cannot differ in bytes and the fingerprint input is canonical.

expiresAt.description: REQUIRED semantics: mode:always defaults to grantedAt+180d (prefs-adjustable down); mode:session expires at session end; mode:once at first use. Absent only for the two non-persistent modes where the runtime derives it. MUST be later than grantedAt (runtime/V35 temporal invariant).

revokedAt.description: MUST be at or after grantedAt (runtime/V35 temporal invariant).

boundClient.description: the client this grant is bound to (§53.4.7)

boundProvider.description: the provider/endpoint this grant is bound to; fingerprint mismatch ⇒ downgrade

osUser.description: OS user profile the grant was issued under (§53.4.7); a different profile never inherits it

docScope.description: the binding scope of the grant. `global` is permitted ONLY for scope:read_document (schema-enforced below, AI-001); a mutating/exporting/network grant must be bound to a named document or workspace.

documentId.description: REQUIRED when docScope=document (AI-001): a document-scoped grant must name the actual document it is bound to, not merely the scope word.

workspaceId.description: REQUIRED when docScope=workspace (AI-002): a workspace-scoped grant must name the actual workspace (§30.3) it is bound to, so the fingerprint binds that workspace and no other.

fingerprint.description: blake3-256 hex (64 lowercase hex chars) over (boundClient tuple incl. installationId+executableFingerprint ‖ boundProvider.endpointFingerprint ‖ boundProvider.credentialPrincipalFingerprint ‖ boundTransport ‖ osUser ‖ docScope ‖ documentId|workspaceId ‖ scope) — the single value the runtime re-checks before honoring a persistent grant (§53.4.7)

allOf.$comment: AI-002 (enforced): a persistent (mode:always) grant MUST carry an explicit expiresAt — a persistent grant that never expires is exactly the failure mode §53.4.7 forbids.

AI-004 (enforced): boundClient.transport and boundTransport must AGREE — the schema ties them together per transport value, so a grant cannot claim one transport in its client tuple and another in its top-level binding.

oneOf.$comment: AI-003 canonical binding branch 1: document-scoped — documentId REQUIRED, workspaceId FORBIDDEN.
branch 2: workspace-scoped — workspaceId REQUIRED, documentId FORBIDDEN.
branch 3: global — ONLY for read_document (AI-001), and NO binding ids may ride along.

auditEntry.$comment: AI-005 (enforced): actor, egressClasses and taintLabels are REQUIRED on every entry (both arrays MAY be empty, but the auditor must state them explicitly — silence is not 'no egress'). grantFingerprint is required whenever outcome=ok (see allOf).

tool.description: tool name, or a §53.4.6 userOperation id (plan.approve, plan.reject, plan.step_confirm, grant.respond, grant.revoke, session.stop)

actor.description: user-plane operations (§53.4.6) record actor:user and are never model-attributable

paramsHash.description: blake3-256 hex (64 lowercase hex chars) of canonical-JSON params — a real digest, never a placeholder (AI-006)

commandIds.description: envelope ids (UUIDv4, §10.2) of commands actually dispatched. v5.5 (AI-005): strictly typed — UUID pattern, no empty strings, no duplicates.

egressClasses.description: §53.14 data-egress contract — which content classes THIS tool call transmitted to a provider (empty for local-only/no-network calls). Machine-checkable against the §53.14 table. AI-006 (enforced): entries are unique, and `none` is EXCLUSIVE — it may only appear alone; an entry cannot claim both 'no egress' and an egress class.

taintLabels.description: §53.5/§53.15 taint provenance present in this call's context: the {source,path} labels that reached the model, so an audit reader can see WHY a tier gate fired. AI-006: entries are unique.

path.description: document path the labeled value came from (e.g. a layerId)

grantFingerprint.description: the §53.4.7 blake3-256 hex fingerprint of the grant that authorized THIS call. REQUIRED for outcome=ok AND outcome=dry_run (a dry run reads protected data); refusals and errors may omit it.

prevHash.description: blake3-256 hex of the previous entry's canonical JSON (chain genesis = blake3 of the sessionId, §53.10.3). AI-006 (enforced): a real 64-hex digest, never a placeholder.

allOf.$comment: AI-005/AI-006 (enforced): a successful call AND a dry run must be attributable to a specific grant — a dry run reads and processes protected document data, so outcome∈{ok,dry_run} requires grantFingerprint; refusals and errors may omit it.
